title: Require table-session verification before QR ordering

completed: reviewed printed QR token, active table-session lifecycle, public actions and POS queue callers
implemented HMAC confirmation code, request JWT and table-session JWT bound to restaurant, table, active session, request and device hash
implemented table-scoped HttpOnly cookie transport without exposing the signed session token in GraphQL
restricted unverified static QR access from order details, order submission, identity OTP, staff call and payment request
added POS in-person verification cards with hidden confirmation codes and matching request labels
limited confirmation attempts to five per request token in five minutes
prevented available or reserved tables from bootstrapping a session before staff marks the table occupied
added backend and frontend regression test files for token scope, cookie scope, bootstrap rules, resolver guards, customer gate and POS code reveal
notes: GitHub connector does not expose a runnable checkout or browser; a container network attempt could not resolve github.com.
One newly confirmed device becomes the active QR-order device for the current table session; confirming another device invalidates the previous device.
The five-attempt limiter is process-local and suitable for the thesis demo; a shared Redis limiter is required for horizontally scaled production.
The printed QR remains long-lived but can only identify the table and request an in-person verification code.
An occupied walk-in table may create an empty table_session for verification; reserved and available tables require staff to open service first.
